lectures.title: How to Measure the Code using Big O?

cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to look at how can we measure the codes using Big-O.
So till now we have learned.
So till now we have learned different types of the time complexities.
Now we are going to look them in practice.
So to make our life easier, I have created a list of rules which will help you when you analyze any
code.
So these are the main rules that you need when you are analyzing the any given code.
Now the first rule is that any assignment statement and if statements that are executed once, regardless
of the size of the problem, will take only one time complex.
So whenever you see if statement or assignment statement, you need to know that this is going to be
a one time complexity.
Now the second rule is that a simple for loop from zero to n with no internal loops will take on time
complex.
So if there is a simple loop without any nested loop, it is on time complexity.
Now the third rule is that if there is another loop inside any given loop, it's going to be o n squared
time complexity.
So we are calling this quadratic time complexity.
Now the fourth rule is a loop in which the controlling parameter is divided by two at each step takes
logarithmic time complexity.
So it's going to be O log n.
Now the last rule is that when dealing with multiple statements together, we are just going to add
them up together.
So these are the common rules that you need when you analyze any given code.
Now let's look at them in one example.
So here we have a function which is taking as a parameter n.
Then it is summing up the numbers from zero until this number.
And then after finding the total it is going to check that if total is more than 100, it's going to
say that the total number is greater than 100.
Otherwise it's going to print out the total number to the console.
So let's see what is the time complexity for this function.
So as I mentioned before we have to analyze these codes separately.
So we are going to look at the first one.
Now in the first line we have created variable.
And we have set zero to this total variable.
And this is going to be assignment statement.
So we have learned that according to our first rule it's going to take zero one time complexity.
Now then we have for loop.
Now we have learned that for loop without any nested loop will take o n time complexity.
So this is going to be rule two.
so it will be on time complexity.
Now inside this loop we have an assignment statement.
We are summing up the numbers.
So this single assignment statement will take all one time complexity.
Now if we combine them we are going to eliminate non-dominant terms which is going to be O one.
And it's going to be on time complexity.
Then we will continue to the next line of code in the next line of code we have if statement.
So if statement says that if total is greater than 100.
So according to our first rule, if statements will take over one time complexity, then we are printing
to the console.
So this one also will take O one time complexity.
Then we will have another console.log.
So this one also will take O one time complexity.
Then according to our fifth rule, when we are dealing with multiple statements, we just need to add
them up.
So in this case I'm just going to add them up.
And we are going to eliminate this constant terms from here.
And it will be on time complexity.
So the time complexity for this simple function is o n.
Because the main factor over here is we are looping from zero until the n that is provided over here,
and it will take all n time complexity.
Now hopefully these five rules will make your life easier when you are finding the time complexity for
any given piece of code.
